title: Machine-learning feature selection identifies student-performance factors in Nepal
summary: A study analyzed 1,021 survey responses from engineering students reflecting on their first year at colleges affiliated with Tribhuvan University in Nepal. A feature-selection vote including Random Forest and AdaBoost selected 21 candidate academic, psychometric and demographic factors, triangulated with 11 focus-group themes and expert review. The reported set included adaptation, motivation, residence and travel-time factors alongside academic measures. These context-dependent selections do not establish causal effects, externally validated predictive performance or transfer beyond the sampled institution system.
ai_technology: Random Forest and AdaBoost within a multi-method feature-selection vote

evidence.tested: Survey data contained 1,021 valid responses; quantitative feature selection used a voting threshold of three and produced 21 features, which were triangulated with 11 focus-group themes and expert review. Fourteen selected features were academic, four psychometric and three demographic.
evidence.unknown: Single-context sample from IOE-affiliated Tribhuvan University colleges; qualitative collection may contain bias; the authors explicitly say the selected determinants are not causal. No external prediction-performance validation is reported.
evidence.ai_role: Random Forest and AdaBoost were included in a multi-method feature-selection vote used to derive the reported student-performance correlates; qualitative focus-group themes and expert review were then used to triangulate them.

source_review.scope: Original journal PDF: posting and peer-review metadata, cohort/data collection, six-method feature-selection vote, triangulation, result categories and conclusions.
